question: Which railway station is a part of UNESCO's world heritage sites?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** (CSMT) is one of the most iconic landmarks in Mumbai, India.
 
• It is a historic railway station and a fine example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India.
 
• CSMT was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 2004 due to its outstanding universal value.
 
• The station was originally named **Victoria Terminus** in honor of Queen Victoria but was renamed in 1996 to its present name.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**

 
 
• The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) designates certain places on Earth as World Heritage Sites.
 
• These sites are selected based on their cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
• Being listed as a World Heritage Site signifies the international recognition of the site's value and the commitment to its preservation.
 
 
 
• **Victorian Gothic Revival Architecture:**
 
 
• This architectural style was prominent in the mid to late 19th century.
 
• It is characterized by features such as pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses.
 
• Buildings in this style often have intricate details and ornamentation, which are evident in CSMT's design.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of CSMT:**
 
 
• CSMT serves as the headquarters of the Central Railways in India.
 
• It was designed by British architect Frederick William Stevens and took over 10 years to complete.
 
• The station remains one of the busiest in India, serving millions of passengers each day.
